video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Portland Trail Blazers 116, San Antonio Spurs 111 | Nov. 25, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's commitment to ball movement and player development
quotes.excerpt: We don't need home runs. We just need more singles and just make the easy play.
quotes.quote: I think that we always talk about, and Gill and his staff in player development do a really good job about talking about pictures, just keeping it simple and all the short-sided games and all the CLA stuff and putting them in position and then just seeing what you see. The thing we talked about with these guys tonight was, we don't need home runs. We just need more singles and just make the easy play. Just get yourself downhill. If Wembanyama presents himself early, kick it to the corner, which we did a phenomenal job of. We get up 53s and we make 19 of them, and we end up with 28 assists all the while shooting 31 free throws. So, I think that's what I attribute it to is just everybody played within themselves, didn't try and do too much, and that's why we were able to take care of it.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the Blazers offensive approach against the Spurs: We don't need home runs. We just need more singles and just make the easy play. Just get yourself downhill.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's offensive strategy of making simple plays and kicking the ball out when Victor Wembanyama defends the paint.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's emotional composure and late-game execution
quotes.excerpt: We talked about playing with emotion, but don't play emotional.
quotes.quote: We talked about it. This team, and good for them, they ended both of our seasons last year, meaning the Trail Blazers and my season, and then they embarrassed us last time they were here. So, we talked about playing with emotion, but don't play emotional. And when Wemby got the big one, he was, he was super excited, but we kept our composure. Then we come down and like you said, Drew, Drew made big threes all night. So whenever we needed one, he just seemed to hit a big one. And then Dame, he hit that one and then he hit the one coming out of the timeout that was huge. But anytime you can string together eight points in that regard, as well as get stops and try to get a little bit of separation, you have to make it a two-possession game against these guys because obviously Wemby, and we've seen it, these guys are all really super talented and they can, if it's a one-possession game, anything can happen. And you even see the putback by Champagnie. So the combination of being able to put together that 8-0 run gave us a little bit of separation and a little bit of wiggle room.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the late game execution against San Antonio: We talked about playing with emotion, but don't play emotional. We kept our composure.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains how the team maintained composure against Victor Wembanyama and relied on key shots from Damian Lillard to secure the win.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Damian Lillard's defensive effort and leadership
quotes.excerpt: I didn't know we'd be talking about Dame Lillard for defensive player of the year.
quotes.quote: I tell you, I don't know if you guys, somebody posted something and he sent it to us on some tweet. I don't know what the number meant, the negative whatever, but all I know is it said Wemby, Thompson, Dame Lillard, really Rudy Gobert. So, I didn't know we'd be talking about Dame Lillard for defensive player of the year, but I just thought he competed his butt off, got into the ball, did a really good job on a couple of isolations even versus Castle and all that. And he has really made it a point to not be, quote-unquote, to be that guy. And he has been phenomenal as far as with his defensive effort and even there down the stretch at the end of the game, he was cursing at me a little bit because he wanted to stay in, but my dumbass took him out. But anyways, he's been really good at that end.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Damian Lillard's defensive effort: I did not know we would be talking about Dame Lillard for defensive player of the year, but I just thought he competed his butt off.

structured.context: Micah Nori praises Damian Lillard for his defensive effort and commitment to playing hard on that end of the floor.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's offensive strategy and defensive pressure
quotes.excerpt: We weren't necessarily making it a point of emphasis to shoot up to shoot 53s.
quotes.quote: They do a really good job because what they try to do, like a lot of teams, and we do the same things, try to play everything two-on-two, funnel it down to Wemby and then stay home on shooters and then make you have to take mid-range and bad shots over top of Wemby. But what happened was we were able to break down their initial pressure, not always with a pick and roll, and then Wemby had to come over and help and then we were able and the which chain reaction started opening up some things. And then not only that, but we were also able, I mean, Dame, off the dribble, some offensive rebound kickouts, you know, those are really tough to stop for them if you're not all the way up at the level. But we weren't necessarily making it a point of emphasis to shoot up to shoot 53s, but we made a point of emphasis was with if you see Wemby in the paint and you don't have a straight line to finish, to find the kickout and make the right play.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the offensive strategy against Victor Wembanyama: If you see Wemby in the paint and you do not have a straight line to finish, find the kickout and make the right play.

structured.context: Micah Nori breaks down how the team successfully countered the defensive pressure applied by the opponent around Victor Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's resilience and growth this season
quotes.excerpt: I'm never satisfied, but I couldn't be happier if that makes sense.
quotes.quote: I would have, quite honestly, I probably would have said let's start the season right now. I see you guys here, quite honestly. And I think the one thing that we were able to do with the way the schedule was, everybody's going to go through it, but I'm actually, well, you know, it's easy to say now that you're 12 and 6 and getting ready to play a boatload of home games and you've played some really tough teams, but just credit to these guys, and then all you guys know it, I mean, we could very easily be, could have should have would have, 14 and 4, whatever you want to say. But to be 12 and 6 with the schedule that we've played as a new group, with the injury to Ja and everybody's had injuries, I just could not be, we're never satisfied, but I couldn't be happier if that makes sense. I just really proud of the group and our guys and the way they've bought in and and it's good.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the Blazers 12 and 6 start: We could very easily be 14 and 4. I could not be happier. I am just really proud of the group and our guys and the way they have bought in.

structured.context: Micah Nori reflects on the team's 12-6 start to the season despite navigating a difficult schedule and injuries to key players like Ja Morant.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team's culture and belief in winning
quotes.excerpt: We don't win by happenstance. We win because we are a top 10 defensive team.
quotes.quote: I think a couple things. One, because I want those guys and I think they are, and I think they and I think they know it, but you guys have been around me enough, I'm not an egotistical person, I'm not a rah-rah type guy, but I just, but I do believe in that group and that locker room. I said that more for them than anybody, that expect to win. We don't win by happenstance. We win because we are a top 10 defensive team and we're a top 10 offensive team and it doesn't matter that we've had some injuries, everybody's had injuries and even you could say we've won some games that maybe if everybody was healthy we may not have, but I just honestly believe because the way our depth is, the way our pieces work, the leadership that we have, the way the guys go about their business, my job is very, very easy because I never have to coach effort. All we have to do is put these guys in the right spots, there's tremendous amount of buying, they all winning is the most important thing and when that happens and you really don't care who gets the credit and all you care about is winning, things are going to go good for you.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the team culture: My job is very, very easy because I never have to coach effort. All we have to do is put these guys in the right spots.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's culture and the players' collective commitment to winning over individual recognition.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Wembanyama's unique impact on the game
quotes.excerpt: When you have no fear that anyone can block your shot, that's a compliment to him.
quotes.quote: I mean, 44 points, but I guess if the, I mean, man oh man, he's, he's a problem. You know, Dwayne Casey used to always talk about Kevin Durant, meaning the rim is always open because he's seven foot and the way he shoots the ball. It's the same thing for Wemby. Like when you have no fear that anyone can block your shot, and that's not a detriment to him, that's a compliment to him and he just got himself to his spots, he found in rhythm. All we tried to do is make it difficult and I mean, he goes 17 for 33, 9 for 9 from three, he made some tough ones. When you go 14 for 21 on twos, I don't know what he was at the rim and then you give him 10 free throws, I just, he is an absolute problem and he is what I think he's done again, credit to him, every year he's been in the league, he has taken better and better shots, I feel like he's got himself to his spot and he just taking what the defense gives him and again, compliment to him, but a compliment to our guys to continue to just stay with it, stay with it, stay with it and end up coming out on top.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Victor Wembanyama after his 44 point performance: Man oh man, he is a problem. When you have no fear that anyone can block your shot, that is a compliment to him.

structured.context: Micah Nori describes the unique challenges of defending Victor Wembanyama and compares his impact to Kevin Durant.
